clue.text: Feature of Trump and PM putting the Queen off

indicators.note: putting something off here means taking it away, so the Queen's letters go from the prime minister's name

parts.note: Margaret Thatcher was a British Prime Minister
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: A comparison of two politicians' looks, with royalty dismissed from the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A thick mop of hair is jokingly called a thatch, and Trump's distinctive hair is famous.

clue.text: Person who is horrible, just a bit, about nothing

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the small amount goes round the zero

parts.note: a tad is a very small amount
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone is only slightly nasty, and over nothing at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling someone a toad is a common insult for a loathsome, repellent person.

clue.text: A short song about aged Greek

indicators.note: about means going round, so the shortened song encloses the age abbreviation
short means cut off at the end, so the song loses its last letter

parts.note: a chant is a song
ae. (aetatis) is the abbreviation for aged, used for someone's age

explanation.surface: A brief tune about an old Greek man.
explanation.walkthrough: AE for 'aged' comes from the Latin aetatis, seen on old portraits and tombstones giving a person's age.
explanation.definitionFit: The Achaeans were the Greeks of Homer's epics, so the word serves as a poetic name for a Greek.

clue.text: Fellow curtly abandoning diocese and ecclesiastical groups

parts.note: a chap is a fellow, a man

indicators.note: abandoning means leaving out, so the diocese name is dropped from the adverb

parts.note: tersely means curtly, briefly
Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire and a diocese

explanation.surface: A man brusquely quits his diocese and the church bodies within it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoning' removes ELY from TERSELY, leaving TERS.
explanation.definitionFit: A cathedral's chapter is its body of canons, so the plural names several church governing bodies.

clue.text: Takes apart splinter group in contemptuous talk

indicators.note: in means placed within, so the faction sits inside the slang word

parts.note: diss is slang for disrespectful or contemptuous talk
a sect is a breakaway faction

explanation.surface: Someone demolishes a breakaway faction with sneering words.
explanation.definitionFit: To dissect is to cut something up or analyse it piece by piece.

clue.text: One caught entering square reprimanded, treated as trash?

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: entering means going inside, so the caught letter goes into the square number

parts.note: nine is a square number, three times three
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
to rate someone is an old word for scolding them

explanation.surface: Someone collared in the town square is told off and handled like rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entering' puts C inside NINE to give NCINE. 'Square' looks like the town square, but it is a number.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubbish is often burnt, so being reduced to ashes is a playful sense of being treated as waste.

clue.text: Being obsequious would put Mrs May off

indicators.note: off means out of order, so the letters of the name are rearranged

explanation.surface: Fawning flattery is what would put the former prime minister off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges MRSMAY. Theresa May was a British Prime Minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone smarmy is oily and ingratiating, the manner of a fawning flatterer.

clue.text: Small room, not half brilliant for accommodating superior writer

indicators.note: accommodating means housing, so the shortened word holds the other letters
not half means only half survives, so the second half of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: clever means brilliant
U stands for upper class, superior
Bic is a brand of ballpoint pen, a writer

explanation.surface: A tiny room, only half bright, where a superior author is put up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'writer' looks like an author, but it is a pen.
explanation.definitionFit: A cubicle is a small partitioned space, such as one for changing or working.

clue.text: Renders Happy Birthday, say, with nicely introduced bumps

indicators.note: introduced means brought in, so the adverb is set inside the verb

parts.note: rendering a song such as Happy Birthday means singing it
well means nicely

explanation.surface: A birthday song performed sweetly, oddly accompanied by lumps.
explanation.definitionFit: Swellings are raised lumps on the body, the same as bumps.

clue.text: Building block of wood, what's backed with board in port

parts.note: ash is a timber, a wood

indicators.note: what comes before the given word: the part of the port word that is followed by board is kept, the rest dropped

parts.note: larboard is the old word for port, the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: A wooden block is described by what lies behind boards in a harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'what's backed with board' takes BOARD off LARBOARD, leaving LAR. 'Port' looks like a harbour; it is the side of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashlar is squared, dressed stone used as a masonry block in building.

clue.text: Able to move quickly for a take-off in an emergency

indicators.note: one thing for another means swapping them, so the quick-move word replaces the article inside the word

parts.note: scram means to get away fast

explanation.surface: A craft that can move fast is ready to lift off in a crisis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' signals SCRAM standing in place of A in ABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Fighter pilots scramble when ordered into the air at once, an urgent launch.

clue.text: Old Testament book's terribly crude and emotional

indicators.note: terribly suggests something badly done, so the letters are mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A reviewer complains that a book of the Bible is vulgar and overwrought.
explanation.definitionFit: Deuteronomy is the fifth Old Testament book, and the adjective means relating to it.

clue.text: Untidy employees making a contribution to Warwickshire's coat of arms

definitions.text: contribution to Warwickshire's coat of arms

parts.note: ragged means scruffy, untidy
staff are a firm's employees

explanation.surface: Scruffy workers add something to the county's heraldic design.
explanation.walkthrough: Warwickshire is an English county whose emblem is the bear and ragged staff, a chained bear holding a knotted branch.
explanation.definitionFit: The knobbly branch in Warwickshire's bear emblem is a heraldic charge in the county arms.

clue.text: Bother in big house having a plant with narcotic properties

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the nuisance goes within the big house

parts.note: a manor is a large country house
a drag is a nuisance, a bother

explanation.surface: Trouble in a stately home that grows a drug-producing plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Mandragora, or mandrake, is a plant whose root has sedative and narcotic effects.

clue.text: Crowd is idle, wandering round, to be got going

parts.note: a mob is a crowd

indicators.note: wandering round means moving about aimlessly, so the letters are shifted into a new order

explanation.surface: An idle crowd roaming about needs to be stirred into action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be' only links; 'got going' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To mobilise troops or people is to set them in motion, to get them moving.

clue.text: Worry when study is neglected in research establishment

indicators.note: neglected means left out, so the study word is removed from the worry word

parts.note: concern means worry
to con is to study or learn

explanation.surface: Anxiety grows when lab work is ignored at a scientific institute.
explanation.definitionFit: CERN is the European particle physics laboratory near Geneva, a major research centre.

clue.text: Lacking special apparel, knight is thrown out, not admired

indicators.note: thrown out means expelled, so the knight letter is removed

parts.note: unadorned means without decoration or finery
N is the chess abbreviation for knight

explanation.surface: A knight without his finery is expelled and nobody admires him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is thrown out' removes N from UNADORNED.
explanation.definitionFit: Unadored means not loved or worshipped, the opposite of being adored.

clue.text: One of two Nobel physicists said to swank

indicators.note: said means spoken, so the physicist's surname is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: William Henry and William Lawrence Bragg, father and son, shared the 1915 Nobel Prize in Physics

explanation.surface: A Nobel-winning scientist is accused of showing off.
explanation.definitionFit: To swank is to show off, to boast about oneself.

clue.text: What could play music in particular key, hard stuff

parts.note: Alt is a key on a computer keyboard
horn is the hard material of animal horns and hooves

explanation.surface: Music is played in a given key and something tough is involved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'key' looks musical; it is the Alt key on a keyboard.
explanation.definitionFit: The althorn is a brass instrument of the saxhorn family, something that plays music.

clue.text: Figures in trouble at sea, reportedly Germanic folk

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard, so the two words are said aloud

parts.note: a wreck is a disaster for a ship
the Angles were a Germanic people who settled in England

explanation.surface: Germanic people in difficulties on the ocean, according to reports.
explanation.definitionFit: Rectangles are four-sided shapes, geometrical figures.

clue.text: Towel I'd discarded, when lots of bits are dry

definitions.text: when lots of bits are dry

indicators.note: discarded suggests thrown aside in disarray, so the letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone at the beach drops their towel once things have dried off.
explanation.definitionFit: When the sea retreats at ebb, stretches of shore normally underwater are left exposed.

clue.text: Bit of paper stuck on yellow garment worn by some women

parts.note: chad is the bit of paper punched out of a ballot or card
or is the heraldic name for gold or yellow

explanation.surface: A scrap of paper glued to a yellow item of clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A chador is a full-length cloak worn by some Muslim women, especially in Iran.

clue.text: Disappoint others giving first instruction to unload the truck?

definitions.text: first instruction to unload the truck?
definitions.meaning: literally, the first step in unloading a lorry is to drop its side panel

explanation.surface: A haulier fails colleagues by giving the opening order for unloading.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means failing your team, and read literally it describes lowering a lorry's tailboard.

clue.text: Like school pupil sounding unrelaxed

indicators.note: sounding means heard aloud, so the word for having been instructed is spoken

parts.note: a pupil is taught at school

explanation.surface: A schoolchild sounds tense.
explanation.definitionFit: Taut means stretched tight, tense rather than slack.

clue.text: Sunday cruciverbalist, maybe, who has cutting edge?

parts.note: a crossword setter or solver is an example of a wordman, someone skilled with words

explanation.surface: A weekend crossword compiler is praised for being sharp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting edge' looks like innovation; here it is a blade.
explanation.definitionFit: A swordsman wields a blade, so he literally has a cutting edge.

clue.text: Symphony offering racy stuff (not Beethoven's Fourth)

indicators.note: not means without, so the chosen letter is dropped from the racy word

parts.note: erotica is sexually explicit writing or art

indicators.note: fourth picks out the fourth letter of the composer's name

explanation.surface: A Beethoven symphony offering spice, though not his Fourth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fourth' takes T, the fourth letter of BEETHOVEN; 'not' removes it from EROTICA. 'Beethoven's Fourth' looks like his fourth symphony.
explanation.definitionFit: The Eroica is Beethoven's Third Symphony, named for heroism.

clue.text: Last thing you want in head and on collar?

definitions.text: Last thing you want in head and on collar?

indicators.note: the last thing of a word is its final letter

parts.note: a ruff is a frilled collar

explanation.surface: Something nobody wants on their scalp or shoulders.
explanation.definitionFit: Dandruff is flakes of dead skin from the scalp that fall onto clothing, unwelcome on both.

clue.text: Commercial to air in busy shopping season

parts.note: an ad is a commercial
to vent is to air feelings or let out air

explanation.surface: Television advertising airs during the hectic pre-Christmas shopping period.
explanation.definitionFit: Advent is the period before Christmas, when shops are at their busiest.
